text:
Situation: Diltiazem hydrochloride injection 100 mg (NDC 00409435003, labeler Hospira, Inc.) has been on FDA's discontinuation list since 2018-02-21. As of 2026-10-21 the listing has been active for 104 months. Corvale East holds 97 vials (9.3 days); Corvale General holds 295 vials (20.9 days).

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 976095 at Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262) ended 2016-06-08 and was classified OAI, 623 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to the same plant on 2017-02-14, 372 days before the posting. A later FDA inspection 1064827 at the plant ended 2018-08-15 and was classified OAI, 175 days after the posting.

Our position: The discontinuation is long-standing and no resupply date exists. Corvale General can spare 50 vials of the 100 mg injection while retaining a two-week supply. The transfer would raise Corvale East to approximately 14 days on hand. Alternative vendors (HF Acquisition Co LLC DBA HealthFirst, Medical Purchasing Solutions LLC, ProPharma Distribution) are not on FDA's shortage list today and their labels name no identifiable manufacturing plant.

Recommended actions:
1. Pharmacy director approves transfer of 50 vials of 100 mg injection from Corvale General to Corvale East.
2. Buyer monitors FDA discontinuation list and vendor availability weekly and reports changes to the committee.

Not recommended: Purchasing from the listed alternative vendors at this time due to lack of plant traceability and absence from FDA's shortage list.
